newsitem.title: USA: Illinois sets August vote on Union/CIPSCO merger.
newsitem.headline: Illinois sets August vote on Union/CIPSCO merger.

text.p: The Illinois Commerce Commission (ICC) said it scheduled to vote in August on whether to approve the proposed $4.8 billion merger between Union Electric Co and CIPSCO Inc.
"The commissioners would not be voting until mid-August," said an ICC spokeswoman.
ICC wants to gather more data and testimony whether the combination of the two Midwest utilities would stifle competition in Illinois' electricity industry, she said.
CIPSCO is based in Springfield, Illinois. Union Electric Co headquarters are in St. Louis, Missouri.
"The case has been reopened by the commission. There was no information on market power," she said.
The Union Electric/CIPSCO merger could "alter the picture of utilities in the state," she added.

Interested parties have until May 21 to file comments with ICC on merger's market impact. An ICC hearing examiner or administrative law judge (ALJ) will hold public hearings on the matter in late May to early June.
On Wednesday, a Federal Energy Regulatory Commission ALJ conditionally recommended the commission approve the deal.
The Missouri Public Service Commission approved the merger February 21 on the condition the combined company joins a regional power transmission group.
The Missouri commission wants the company to set a region-wide transmission rate with the group so it could not restrict competition by imposing high power transmission line fees.

The merger of Union Electric and CIPSCO, announced last August, would create a new holding company called Ameren Corp, with annual revenues of nearly $3 billion and over 1.5 million electric customers across Missouri and in central and south-central Illinois.
